It cannot be attributed to a specific seed. provenance.header_bug_note: The CSV header names column 9 'time_norm', but InterviewEnv.step()'s writer actually puts the 'progress' variable (current_step / max_steps) there, not a response-time-normalized value. Verified: this column's observed values are exact multiples of 1/15 (0.0667, 0.1333, ..., 1.0), consistent with max_steps=15 and progress = step/15, not with any time-based quantity. This is a label/content mismatch in the frozen logger itself, harmless to training (the real progress variable is used correctly inside step()), but relevant to anyone reading this column by its header name.

g6_strong_harder.note: g6 fired 0 times in the 5-persona P3 evaluation replay (see the companion guardrail-coverage report); it fires here at a non-trivial rate under the training-matched (skill=0.6, normal) candidate.

forced_action_column_semantics_note: forced_action==True whenever guardrail_id != 'none' (i.e. it means 'a guardrail rule matched', not 'the guardrail changed the action') -- confirmed: forced_action_rate_overall equals guardrail_coverage_overall exactly (0.6129 == 0.6129). The action-changing rate used below is the separately-computed pre_action != action indicator, matching the 'override' definition used in the companion guardrail-coverage-decomposition report.

g6_and_correct_harder_proposals.interpretation: No guardrail ever blocks or changes away from a correct Harder proposal in this log (0 of 34,535 such rows have action != pre_action). g6 fires concurrently with an already-correct Harder proposal in a large share of cases (redundant reconfirmation, the same pattern g5 showed at evaluation time: 0% override rate), and separately forces Harder in the ~37% of its activations where PPO's raw proposal was NOT already Harder (a genuine correction toward the oracle's target, not a block).
